metadata.label: Monochrome
metadata.coverage: Twelve CISSCAL clear-filter observations in the Thomas controlled shape frame, including a regional ~100 m/pixel close frame with independently checked camera correction. Approximate disk correction and overlap levels reduce photographed illumination; shadows, variable resolution and marked gaps remain.

celestial.sunSource: JPL Saturn-system orbital data; the shape uses the controlled Cassini September 2005 frame. Its displayed orientation is arbitrary because Hyperion rotates chaotically.
celestial.qualification: The ephemeris locates the Sun, but Hyperion’s body attitude is an explicitly arbitrary display orientation. Its directional lighting is a display convention, not a prediction of the current tumbling surface phase.

panel.introduction: Hyperion is Saturn’s sponge-like, chaotically tumbling moon. Deep craters cover a porous, irregular body whose dark crater floors contrast with brighter icy walls. The displayed orientation and lighting are illustrative; its chaotic tumbling is not simulated.

facts.label: Discovery
facts.value: William Lassell and William and George Bond · 1848

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.description: Twelve calibrated Cassini frames mapped to the irregular shape, including a regional close view sampled at about 100 m/pixel. Registration and shape uncertainty limit detail; crater shadows remain, coverage varies and gaps are marked.
controls.title: ISS calibrated mosaic
controls.summary: Twelve Cassini frames, including a regional ~100 m/pixel close view. Shape and registration limit detail; shadows and marked gaps remain.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Radius above a 135 km reference sphere from the Cassini stereo and limb shape model. This shows global relief and elongation, not a finely resolved terrain DEM; shape uncertainty reaches 6 km on the less-observed side.
controls.title: Shape-derived radial height
controls.summary: Cassini-model height relative to a 135 km sphere. Shape errors reach 6 km on the less-observed side.
